interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a low-grade prostatectomy (Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2), negative surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles or lymphovascular invasion. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 5.3 and the absence of lymph node removal, as nodal status is not documented, which widens uncertainty. The biopsy finding of a tubular and cribriform pattern was noted. The lack of documented postoperative PSA or follow-up significantly limits the certainty of the trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trend would be crucial in revising this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 85 months without an event, though the uncertainty interval is broad. Missing nodal sampling further complicates the assessment of local control. The fixed estimated horizon is 84.76 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 55.09–114.42 months; its coverage has not been validated.
